title: Owls
passages: Most owls are NOCTURNAL, which means they hunt at night while many other birds sleep. Their huge eyes gather what little light there is, helping them spot movement in the dark. Hearing matters even more. The flat, round face of many owls works like a dish, guiding sound toward their ears. In some kinds of owls, one ear sits higher than the other, so the bird can tell exactly where a tiny noise is coming from. A hunting owl can find a mouse rustling under leaves or even under snow, then drop onto it with sharp TALONS.

An owl cannot roll its eyes the way people can, because its eyes are shaped like tubes and stay fixed in place. Instead, it turns its whole head, up to about three quarters of a full circle. Its neck holds twice as many VERTEBRAE as a human neck. Owls also fly almost without a sound. Tiny SERRATIONS along the front edge of each wing break up rushing air, and soft, velvety feathers muffle the rest. Around the world, people have wondered at these quiet hunters, and many cultures tell stories of owls as wise watchers of the night.
